rows.description: A child follows the sticker chart: brush teeth, finish milk, put shoes in the rack. Each finished task gets a sticker, and ten stickers means a trip to the park.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, if-then plan, magical thinking, negotiation

rows.description: A child says, "If I eat all my vegetables, can I have two stories tonight?" Naming the price and the prize makes the deal explicit.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, if-then plan, impulsive action, magical thinking

rows.description: A child holds the rule, "If I put my toys away, I get a sticker," and does it as soon as playtime ends. The link between action and prize is understood.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, impulsive action, magical thinking, negotiation

rows.description: A child wishes on the first star for extra stickers and expects them to show up on the chart in the morning. The wish is trusted more than the routine.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, if-then plan, impulsive action, negotiation

rows.description: Unsure how far off the reward is, a child asks mother, "How many more stickers?" She counts three with the child, and the goal becomes something concrete.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: if-then plan, impulsive action, magical thinking, negotiation

rows.subtype: Approach: giving up after a miss [Pitfall]
rows.description: After missing two days, a child says the chart is finished and does not try again. One lapse feels like total failure, until a parent restarts the count.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, if-then plan, impulsive action, magical thinking, negotiation

rows.description: A child looks for a lost shoe by going back through the day: the bedroom, the verandah, the gate where she played. Going in order narrows down where it could be.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, copying without fit, magical thinking, mental simulation, trial and error
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12

rows.description: A child says, "Mummy, I can't find my shoe," and mother asks, "Where did you last have it?" The adult's question gives the search a structure.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, magical thinking, mental simulation, trial and error
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12

rows.description: A child pretends to be the missing shoe and asks, "Where would I go?" Imagining its journey brings up the idea of looking under the sofa.

rows.description: A child insists that the shoe "ran away" and that it will come home if she waits at the door. Waiting replaces searching.
